When we submitted these documents to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), our application was resubmitted and rejected, stating that virtual office addresses are not permitted for registration. This clearly shows that Regus misled us into believing it was possible.

We also faced continuous unprofessional and rude behavior from Neelam, who even demanded personal documents like a marriage certificate (which our lawyer later confirmed was unnecessary). She was often unavailable, inflexible with timings, and extremely discourteous.

We have now terminated our agreement and will not be making any further payments, as the service did not meet its stated purpose. We believe Regus is misleading customers by selling virtual offices for company registration when they know MCA does not allow it.

Please be very cautious if you are a startup or a small business trying to register your company — do not waste your money or time with Regus. We are now moving forward with a proper physical office for our company, and I am grateful that MCA did not accept this address — because our experience with Regus was extremely disappointing from the start.
